hypothesis: Expert-mapped new faults (the hidden truth) concentrate as secondary strands in the damage zones of known USGS/INGENIOUS faults: subparallel splays and parallel strands whose distance from the primary trace, azimuth relative to its strike, and along-strike position (beyond-tip extensions) follow shear-zone mechanics, with zone width growing with fault length (displacement proxy). The organizers confirmed a new fault is any fault pixel not already captured by USGS/INGENIOUS, including newly mapped geometry of an existing system, so splays and parallel strands count (thread 11536).
mechanism: Per-fault intensity I(p) = f(d/s(L)) * g(phi), where f is the empirical radial density, g the empirical offset-azimuth density, and s(L) the empirical length scaling (displacement proxy), ALL fitted on the hide-and-recover holdout (random whole-segment folds, 300 m truth buffer, features rebuilt from visible faults only, visible+INGENIOUS faults masked pixel-exactly, pooled DTI alpha=0.2 beta=0.8 R=300 m). No textbook Riedel/Tchalenko angle is hard-coded. Sense of slip is conditioned where the INGENIOUS database records it (RL/LL/N) and kept marginal where it does not (the holdout cannot resolve it: nearest-visible sense unk=38063, N=214, RL=53, LL=9). Emission: binary top-k dots off known faults, k swept on the holdout. The d<3 px band (removed by the holdout's 300 m truth buffer) is extended from the SGMC off-catalogue population and flagged as such.
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Anthropogenic and geomorphic lineaments that parallel mapped faults in the alluvial basins of the northwestern Great Basin: roads, fence lines and powerline alignments, and pluvial-lake shorelines / alluvial-fan risers that follow basin structure subparallel to fault strikes. These cluster near and parallel to mapped fault scarps and would be predicted by the same halo geometry without being faults.

verdict_reasoning: The lane is VALIDATED as a real, non-leaking, unique signal: it beats its own controls on the brief's holdout instrument (0.0580 vs random 0.0492 and uniform-halo 0.0117 at 60k dots), the leakage canary is far below threshold (max AUC 0.6538 < 0.90), and the drift check is clean (max |Spearman| 0.6271 < 0.90, no bidirectional duplicates, sha256 unique across 663 registry rasters). But it does NOT beat the current holdout best on the template instrument (d15 scores 0.0844 as-is on the same folds; comparison is conservative for this lane, whose 0.0580 is per-fold-rebuilt while d15 is a frozen artifact scored as-is), and on the SGMC-truth instrument (the better proxy for the live target) it trails the incumbents 2-3x (0.0457 vs 0.0931-0.1450). As a standalone submission it is therefore not expected to beat the incumbent LIVE 0.2778. Promotion to a real slot is a separate selector step; per the session rule, no slot should be spent on this artifact. The submission file is generated, validated and downloadable (the session's highest-urgency deliverable), and the negative result is the deliverable: the fitted damage zone is real structure, but pure catalogue geometry is not enough - the next step is zone-gated geophysical corroboration (hypothesis H2 in docs/research/hypotheses.md).
